title: Primary Immunodeficiency Screening: TREC, DHR and Antibody Function
summary: Use TRECs to screen newborns for SCID, the DHR flow assay to detect CGD, and immunoglobulin levels with vaccine responses to diagnose CVID — and learn why titres measured on IVIG are borrowed.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 52 Hits 1, 3, 6 and 12 and Trap 2 (first lesson for Ch. 52). Checked against Kwan 2014, Kim 2013 and ICON 2016 (Bonilla). Discrepancies: CVID “age > 2 years” follows the 1999 ESID/PAGID definition, while ICON 2016 advises against diagnosis before at least age 4 (register rv-cvid-age); TRECs are DNA measured by real-time (quantitative) PCR — the reviewer’s “quantitative RT-PCR” should not be read as reverse transcription. Not taught: lymphocyte thresholds, catalase-positive organism list, NBT history, XLA, hyper-IgM/IgE, WAS, DiGeorge, IPEX, bare lymphocyte syndromes, LAD, Chédiak–Higashi, IgA deficiency and blood products, the 5–6-month IVIG hold, gene therapy, IUIS counts, and the all-50-states/May 2010 date.

objectives: Explain what TRECs measure and how a newborn SCID screen is followed up.
Describe the DHR flow assay and what an absent response means.
Apply CVID criteria and explain why vaccine titres on IgG therapy are unreliable.

scenes.title: Three immune puzzles
scenes.altText: Three invented requests reach the immunology bench. (1) Newborn screen: TREC UNDETECTABLE on a dried blood spot. (2) A 3-year-old with recurrent abscesses and a lung fungal infection: “oxidative burst test, please”. (3) A 35-year-old on IVIG for 6 months: “check vaccine titres to confirm antibody deficiency”. Question token: “What does each test measure — and which request has a problem?”

cues.text: Three requests arrive. A newborn’s dried blood spot shows no T-cell receptor excision circles.
A toddler with recurrent abscesses and a fungal lung infection needs an oxidative burst test.
And an adult already on IVIG wants vaccine titres to prove antibody deficiency. What does each test measure, and which request has a problem?

scenes.title: What the normal immune system leaves behind
scenes.altText: TREC card (Kwan 2014): T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) are a biomarker of new T-cell production (T lymphopoiesis); they are DNA, measured by PCR on DNA from newborn dried blood spots. ICON 2016: real-time PCR quantification of TRECs (and KRECs for B cells) is used for newborn screening. Phagocyte card (Kim 2013): the phagocyte NADPH oxidase complex (gp91phox, p22phox, p40phox, p47phox, p67phox) makes superoxide and other reactive oxygen species needed to kill bacteria and fungi. Antibody card (ICON 2016): at birth IgG is high from maternal transfer; levels fall to a nadir at 3–6 months and then rise, so age-related ranges are required.

cues.text: A healthy thymus makes new T cells, and each new T cell leaves behind a small circle of DNA, a TREC. PCR on a newborn blood spot can count them.
Neutrophils kill microbes with an enzyme complex called NADPH oxidase, which makes superoxide and other reactive oxygen species.
Antibody levels change with age. A newborn’s IgG is mostly the mother’s; it falls to a low point at three to six months, then the baby’s own IgG rises.
So every result must be read against age-related reference ranges.

scenes.title: When a piece is missing
scenes.altText: SCID card (Kwan 2014): dried blood spots of apparently healthy newborns later diagnosed with SCID LACKED TRECs; screening 3,030,083 newborns in 11 US programs found SCID in about 1 in 58,000; positive screens go to confirmatory flow cytometry; interventions included transplantation, enzyme replacement or gene therapy, immunoglobulin infusions, preventive antibiotics, and AVOIDING LIVE VACCINES. CGD card (Kim 2013): defects in NADPH oxidase cause impaired superoxide production → life-threatening bacterial and fungal infections and granulomatous inflammation. Antibody card (ICON 2016): CVID — marked decrease of IgG (≥ 2 SD below the age mean) plus low IgM or IgA, with absent isohemagglutinins and/or poor vaccine responses, after other causes are excluded; infections mainly with encapsulated extracellular bacteria; best NOT diagnosed before at least age 4 years.

cues.text: In SCID the thymus makes few or no new T cells, so newborn blood spots lack TRECs. Across eleven US screening programs, SCID turned up in about 1 in 58,000 babies.
A positive screen goes to flow cytometry for confirmation, and affected infants must avoid live vaccines.
In chronic granulomatous disease, a broken NADPH oxidase cannot make superoxide, causing serious bacterial and fungal infections and granulomas.
In common variable immunodeficiency, IgG is markedly low together with IgA or IgM, and vaccine responses or isohemagglutinins are poor. It is a diagnosis of exclusion, best not made before age 4.

scenes.title: Running and reading the tests
scenes.altText: DHR card (Kim 2013): the dihydrorhodamine (DHR) flow cytometry assay detects absent or reduced NADPH oxidase activity in phagocytes STIMULATED with phorbol myristate acetate (PMA); the X-linked CGD patient showed essentially no DHR fluorescence after stimulation (0.2%); the assay also tracked donor neutrophil chimerism after transplantation. Antibody-testing card (ICON 2016): measure IgG, IgM, IgA and IgE against age-related ranges; test specific antibody to protein and polysaccharide vaccines (polysaccharide pneumococcal vaccine usable in adults and children > 12 months); IgG products contain high levels of common vaccine antibodies, so titres measured on IgG therapy are not the patient’s own — interpretation must be adjusted; neoantigen vaccines not previously given (e.g. rabies, tick-borne encephalitis) can test patients already on IgG. Hook answers: (1) TREC absent → confirm by flow cytometry, no live vaccines; (2) DHR after PMA; (3) titres on IVIG mostly reflect donor antibody.

cues.text: For chronic granulomatous disease, the dihydrorhodamine test stimulates neutrophils with PMA and watches for fluorescence by flow cytometry. Normal cells light up; in X-linked CGD there was almost none.
For antibody deficiency, measure IgG, IgM, IgA and IgE against age-related ranges, then test real antibody function with protein and polysaccharide vaccines.
But IgG products contain plenty of antibody to common vaccines, so titres measured during therapy are not the patient’s own. A vaccine the patient has never had, such as rabies, can be used instead.
So: the newborn needs flow cytometry and no live vaccines; the toddler needs a DHR test; and the adult’s titres on IVIG mostly reflect donor antibody.

props.label: Hook: flow + no live vaccines · DHR · titres borrowed

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Good vaccine titres while on IVIG prove intact antibody production” (✓ IgG products contain vaccine antibodies — titres are borrowed; use a neoantigen or adjust interpretation); “An undetectable TREC screen diagnoses SCID” (✓ it is a screen — confirm with flow cytometry; protect from live vaccines meanwhile); “CVID can be diagnosed in a 2-year-old with low IgG” (✓ ICON: best not before at least age 4; IgG naturally dips at 3–6 months and other causes must be excluded).

cues.text: Trap one: good vaccine titres while on IVIG prove the patient makes antibody. No: the product contains those antibodies. The titres are borrowed.
Trap two: an undetectable TREC result diagnoses SCID. No: it is a screen. Confirm with flow cytometry, and avoid live vaccines meanwhile.
Trap three: diagnose CVID in a 2-year-old with low IgG. No: the international consensus advises waiting until at least age 4 and excluding other causes.

scenes.title: Receipts, sparks and borrowed money
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “TRECs are the thymus’s RECEIPTS — no receipts, no new T cells. DHR looks for the SPARK — no spark after PMA, no oxidase. Titres on IVIG are BORROWED MONEY — they don’t show what the patient can earn.” Tokens: TREC = receipts · DHR = spark · IVIG titres = borrowed. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: TRECs are the thymus’s receipts; no receipts, no new T cells. DHR looks for the spark; no spark after PMA, no oxidase. Titres on IVIG are borrowed money; they do not show what the patient can earn.

Where it breaks: low TRECs also occur with conditions other than SCID, and programs have false positives, so confirmation is essential; partial oxidase defects give a reduced rather than absent spark; and some CVID patients still respond to some vaccines.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “No TRECs → confirm by flow, no live vaccines (SCID ~1 in 58,000) · no DHR signal after PMA → CGD (NADPH oxidase)”, “CVID: IgG ↓ + IgA/IgM ↓ + poor responses, after exclusion, best from age ≥ 4 · titres on IVIG are borrowed”.

cues.text: Absent TRECs flag possible SCID for flow-cytometry confirmation, absent DHR fluorescence after PMA points to CGD, and antibody deficiency is judged by immunoglobulin levels plus vaccine responses that cannot be read at face value while a patient is on IgG therapy.

props.label: No TREC → flow + no live vaccines · no DHR after PMA → CGD
CVID: IgG + IgA/IgM ↓ + poor response, age ≥ 4 · IVIG titres borrowed

explanation.what: Plain language: newborn blood spots can show whether the thymus is making new T cells, a light-up test shows whether neutrophils can make their killing chemicals, and antibody tests show whether someone can make their own protective antibodies. Scientific terms: TREC, KREC, T lymphopoiesis, SCID, flow cytometry, NADPH oxidase, superoxide, chronic granulomatous disease (CGD), dihydrorhodamine (DHR), PMA, CVID, isohemagglutinins, polysaccharide and protein vaccine responses, IgG replacement.
explanation.why: TRECs are left over only when new T-cell receptors are made, so their absence means little new T-cell production. Without NADPH oxidase activity, PMA-stimulated phagocytes do not show the DHR fluorescence shift. Donor IgG supplies antibodies to common vaccines, masking the patient’s own response.
explanation.measure: TREC PCR on dried blood spots → flow cytometry confirmation (Kwan 2014). DHR flow assay after PMA (Kim 2013). IgG, IgM, IgA, IgE against age ranges; protein and polysaccharide vaccine responses; neoantigens (rabies, TBE) for patients on IgG (ICON 2016).
explanation.differs: SCID (no TRECs; T-cell production) vs CGD (normal cell numbers, absent oxidative burst) vs CVID (low immunoglobulins with poor specific antibody); patient’s own titres vs titres borrowed from IgG products.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: identify the test for each defect (TREC, DHR, vaccine responses), the next step after an abnormal TREC, CVID criteria, and why titres on IVIG mislead.

questions.stem: A newborn screen reports undetectable TRECs. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Confirm with lymphocyte flow cytometry and avoid live vaccines until resolved
options.rationale: Correct. TREC is a screen; positives are referred for flow cytometry, and live vaccines are avoided.

options.text: Diagnose SCID and start gene therapy immediately
options.rationale: Incorrect. A screen must be confirmed first.
Incorrect. Delay is dangerous; SCID needs early detection.

options.text: Give live rotavirus vaccine to test immunity
options.rationale: Incorrect. Live vaccines are avoided in suspected SCID.

questions.stem: Neutrophils from a boy with recurrent abscesses show no fluorescence shift in the DHR assay after PMA stimulation. Which defect fits?

options.rationale: Correct. DHR detects absent or reduced NADPH oxidase activity in stimulated phagocytes.
Incorrect. That is assessed with TRECs and flow cytometry.

options.text: Low IgG with poor vaccine responses
options.rationale: Incorrect. That describes antibody deficiency such as CVID.
Incorrect. That causes hereditary angioedema, not an absent oxidative burst.

questions.stem: An adult with suspected CVID has been on IVIG for a year. Tetanus and pneumococcal titres are protective. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: The titres may come from the IgG product; assess with a neoantigen vaccine or adjusted interpretation
options.rationale: Correct. IgG products contain high levels of common vaccine antibodies (ICON 2016).
Incorrect. The measured antibody may be donor-derived.

options.text: CVID is excluded because IgG is now normal
options.rationale: Incorrect. IgG levels on replacement reflect the product.
Incorrect. Repetition does not separate donor from patient antibody.

accuracyFlags.issue: The reviewer gives CVID diagnosis as requiring “age > 2 years”, which is the 1999 ESID/PAGID definition. ICON 2016 recommends not conferring the diagnosis before at least age 4 years.

The reviewer says TRECs are measured by “quantitative RT-PCR”. TRECs are DNA circles measured by real-time (quantitative) PCR on DNA from dried blood spots (Kwan 2014; ICON 2016); RT-PCR usually denotes reverse transcription of RNA.
